body.x: Greneta Corporation (CEO TaeWoong Kim) announced its participation in CES 2025, which will be held from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas. The company will exhibit at the K-Startup Pavilion and present its innovative 3D content creation and distribution platform, Keeep.

Greneta specializes in simplifying the production, sale, and use of high-quality 3D content in mobile environments through Keeep. By streamlining traditionally complex 3D object creation processes, the platform has gained strong support from users across various industries.

The company aims to connect 3D scanning professionals and novice users while revolutionizing 3D data transactions and the creation of ecosystems. Greneta is also preparing to launch integrated services with leading XR platform Meta to allow seamless use of data generated on Keeep in both real and virtual spaces.
At CES 2025, Greneta plans to showcase Keeep before its global launch to maximize market opportunities.

A standout feature of Keeep is its lightweight data compression technology, which reduces 3D data sizes to one-hundredth of the original volume while maintaining visual quality. This allows smooth data sharing and distribution across various networks and hardware environments and excellent compatibility with other platforms.

The platform also features automated 3D architecture generation, significantly reducing production time from five days to 30 seconds. This rapid creation process and high diversity support efficient data use in architecture, gaming, education, and more.

Keeep also includes a Three.js-based web viewer that enables real-time quality checks and reviews, facilitating seamless data trading and distribution between individuals and organizations. Through these capabilities, Greneta aims to empower global creators in 3D content production and transactions while leading the future of digital content.

Greneta has partnered with major domestic construction firms to provide digital twin solutions, enhancing efficiency in installation inspections, design history management, and maintenance inspections. The company is also working on automating its data compression algorithm for 3D scan data and providing API solutions compatible with any web environment.

A Greneta representative commented, “Our technology dramatically reduces the costs of processing, transmitting, and managing digital twin data, and we have worked with various customer groups. At CES 2025, we expect to create new opportunities, particularly in markets with high demand for 3D content.”

The representative added, “Our goal is to secure customers in the U.S., known for its vibrant 3D content market, Japan, with its strong demand for high-quality digital content, and Europe, which has growing interests in XR content diversification, digital cultural heritage preservation, and architectural design.”

AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. To promote Korean startups worldwide, AVING will host its Broadcasting Zone at the Venetian Expo, featuring the CES Media Day Startup Conference and global media interviews.
